newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end down, foreign funds stay sellers.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end down, foreign funds stay sellers.

text.p: Indian shares ended lower on Monday as punters hammered prices and foreign funds offloaded select stocks including cement maker ACC, traders said.
"The market was looking extremely weak," said a National Stock Exchange (NSE) trader at a foreign brokerage.
NSE's 50-stocks index ended 19 points lower at 962.27
"Most domestic institutions were closed. There was some selling by foreign funds but most of the volumes were driven by operators," the trader said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange and some regional stock exchanges remained closed for a Hindu festival.
A technical analyst at a local brokerage said Bombay's benchmark index was headed towards 3100 points in the coming weeks. The index ended 44.17 points down at 3347.37 on Friday.
"We might hit a bottom quicker if the market sees a panic sell-off but a slow erosion with an intermittent rally could be dangerous for the market," the analyst said.
Last week, Bombay's benchmark index slumped 160.70 points or 4.8 percent to 3347.37 after the government failed to deliver anticipated tax reliefs.
Cement maker ACC fell 81 rupees or 4.10 percent to close at 1,897 on the NSE as a foreign fund offloaded the stock.

Analysts say a series of cost increases including fuel, freight and power have led to escallating production costs at a time when signs of oversupply in the cement sector are evident in several regions.
Shares of truckmaker TELCO fell 6.80 rupees to 450 on reports of a slowdown in sales. Auto analysts say sales of light commercial vehicles are likely to pick up in September.
Delhi shares ended lower in new-account trade with the index down 1.18 points at 736.84.
In Calcutta, the index fell 4.81 points to 430.23.
